# `unwaited-child-process`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a child returned by `std.process.spawn` that reaches the end of its
scope without `wait`, `kill`, or ownership transfer.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

An unwaited child retains process status and associated OS resources after it
exits.

## When it fires

Wait for or kill the child in the same scope, or transfer the child value to an
owner whose lifetime contract includes that operation.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn launch(io: std.Io, wait_for_it: bool) !void {
    var child = try std.process.spawn(io, .{ .argv = &.{"true"} });
    if (wait_for_it) {
        _ = try child.wait(io);
    }
}
```
